rooms.name: Petition Steps
rooms.description: A groove runs down the centre of the steps where people pushed written petitions under the door.

encounters.cue: Inspect the narrow groove under the door.
encounters.result: A sliver of folded linen is caught at the bend. Paper wore through on the stone, so some petitioners wrapped their letters.

rooms.name: Records Porch
rooms.description: Umbrellas dry above a locked drawer full of unanswered claims. The register clerk takes visitors through the side arch.

encounters.cue: Read the tags on the umbrella hooks.
encounters.result: Each carries a claim number in pencil. People expected to be back for their umbrellas long before the numbers faded.

rooms.name: Index Hall
rooms.description: A sliding index sorts the missing under the names of their employers. Someone has added a drawer for children.

encounters.cue: Look at the runners beneath the children's drawer.
encounters.result: The runners are made from reversed ruler strips. From underneath you can read the height marks of children who once used them.

rooms.name: Ink Kitchen
rooms.description: Gallnuts simmer beside an iron spoon worn to a ring. This ink turns brown precisely where older names have been erased.

encounters.cue: Inspect the spoon beside the gallnuts.
encounters.result: Its missing bowl left a perfect ring for lifting a drop. The clerk could test a small erasure without staining the whole page.

rooms.name: Blotting Loft
rooms.description: Reversed letters on the drying sheets spell out part of a warning about the lower dam seat.

encounters.cue: Read the darkest blot in reverse.
encounters.result: Beneath the warning someone added a plea to send a second copy by hand. The ink soaked through three drying sheets.

rooms.name: Map Press
rooms.description: A pressed survey traces a thin return conduit around the dam. Its surveyor drew a thumb beside the difficult turn.

encounters.cue: Look closely at the thumb on the pressed survey.
encounters.result: Fine hatch marks run across the drawn thumbnail. The surveyor used its width for scale where a ruler could not follow the turn.

rooms.name: Seal Room
rooms.description: The city seal is a two-faced stamp. The face for emergency orders has a broken tooth.

encounters.cue: Compare the damaged tooth with the practice seals.
encounters.result: The practice wax carries the same tiny gap. It gives the clerk a way to recognise an emergency seal even when its lettering smears.

rooms.name: Widows' Window
rooms.description: A shelf at elbow height is smooth from years of waiting. Forty years of rain have never reached it.

encounters.cue: Feel beneath the smooth edge of the waiting shelf.
encounters.result: Rows of shallow cuts lie a finger apart. Somebody counted visits on the side the clerk could never see.

rooms.name: Roll Vault
rooms.description: The last shift roll has two leaves sewn together. Warm breath lifts the brittle thread between them.

encounters.cue: Two leaves of the shift roll stick together at the cut edge.
encounters.result: The paired muster names are Wren Above and Pike Below. Ada signed a closure from below to save both shifts; the surface clerk recorded everyone below as lost.

rooms.name: Copy Desk
rooms.description: Tern copies names onto linen so they will survive a flood. The last family on his sheet has no surface address.

encounters.cue: Tern the copyist dots letters with the blunt end of his pen. He wants the lower families back on the rolls.
encounters.result: Tern saw bread billed for a whole street below last winter. The two leaves of the last shift roll can be separated with warm breath.

rooms.name: Tax Cage
rooms.description: An invoice charges the city for lamp oil delivered below the dam last winter.

encounters.cue: Inspect the delivery receipt stapled to the invoice.
encounters.result: A thumbprint in lampblack stands in for a signature. A warm can left a round mark right through the next sheet.

rooms.name: Paper Bridge
rooms.description: Bundles of ruined census forms prop up a short bridge. Faces drawn in the margins look out from underneath.

encounters.cue: Examine the faces under the bridge.
encounters.result: A strip of dry margin joins two portraits hand to hand. Someone folded the ruined returns to keep a family on the same side.

rooms.name: Varnish Closet
rooms.description: Rows of little jars hold seal varnish. One still smells of the resin used by the lower boatbuilders.

encounters.cue: Inspect the stopper on the resin jar.
encounters.result: It is whittled from a boat peg. A faint rope groove was already in the wood before the jar came to the archive.

rooms.name: Appeal Gallery
rooms.description: Each rejected appeal has its own hook. A red cord ties together the hooks for one entire shift.

encounters.cue: Follow the red cord between the hooks.
encounters.result: A separate knot sits at each empty hook. Removing the paper never removed that person's place in the appeal.

rooms.name: Audit Cell
rooms.description: A desk has a glass top so even a hiding clerk could be seen counting. The pencil underneath lists births.

encounters.cue: Read the pencil marks through the desk glass.
encounters.result: The names run backwards. The clerk wrote under the glass so a visitor leaning over the desk could read them.

rooms.name: Rain Gauge
rooms.description: The instrument measures rainfall above the archive. Its scale has been extended downward on a strip of bone.

encounters.cue: Look at the join between bone and brass.
encounters.result: The first division on the bone repeats the last on the brass. The keeper checked the overlap before trusting the lower readings.

rooms.name: Pension Hatch
rooms.description: Pensions were paid in bread here until the same morning every account was closed.

encounters.cue: Look beneath the pension hatch.
encounters.result: A floury stamp shaped like half a loaf is wedged in the rail. A half share once had to be accounted for as carefully as a whole one.

rooms.name: Bell Ordinance
rooms.description: The bronze ordinance grants the person below the right to request a halt. No line says a surface officer must agree.

encounters.cue: Examine the high letters of the bronze ordinance.
encounters.result: Black wax remains around the raised words. Workers took rubbings small enough to fold inside a cap.

rooms.name: Archive Lift
rooms.description: A goods cage smells of warm pottery. Copies of the survey travelled by this route to the kilns.

encounters.cue: Inspect the narrow batten across the goods cage.
encounters.result: A flat gap below it fits a rolled survey but stops a pottery jar. The cage could carry fragile copies and kiln goods on the same trip.

rooms.name: Witness Bench
rooms.description: Two polished seats face each other. The nearer one bears the initials of both keepers who signed the flood order.

encounters.cue: Inspect the initials on the nearer seat.
encounters.result: The cuts face in opposite directions. The keepers sat shoulder to shoulder and each reached across to carve.
